prompt: A $12 \times 8$ rectangle has a $4 \times 4$ square removed from one corner. **Area remaining**?
hint: A corner square has been removed from the rectangle. The area left over is smaller than the full rectangle by exactly that square.

hints.title: 🔁 Another angle
hints.text: Another way is to slice the leftover shape into a $12 \times 4$ rectangle and an $8 \times 4$ rectangle. Their areas add to the same answer.
A corner square has been removed from the rectangle. The area left over is smaller than the full rectangle by exactly that square.
The full rectangle is $12 \times 8 = 96$ and the removed square is $4 \times 4 = 16$. Subtract the square.
$96 - 16 = 80$, so the area remaining is $80$ square units.

explanation: Find the area of the rectangle before the corner is removed: $12 \times 8 = 96$.
Find the area of the removed square: $4 \times 4 = 16$.
Subtract the removed part from the whole: $96 - 16 = 80$.
The area remaining is $80$ square units.

alternativeExplanations.title: Decompose into rectangles
steps: The remaining shape can be split into a $12 \times 4$ and an $8 \times 4$ rectangle.
